contentFull:
BloomX raises $13 million to expand robotic pollination in fruit crops

 19-10 | Smart farming | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

loomX's Yahav 2400 uses an electric field and a specialised textile to collect and transfer pollen between avocado flowers. The system was commercially launched in 2026. Photo: Tzach Gefen/BloomX

Israeli agtech company BloomX has raised $13 million (€11.2 million) to expand its robotic pollination technology for avocado and blueberry growers. The company claims its systems can increase yields by an average of 20% by supplementing natural pollination. BloomX is expanding in Latin America and South Africa and preparing to enter the US market.

BloomX has developed two commercially available pollination systems that mimic the way bees transfer pollen between flowers. Rather than replacing natural pollinators, the machines are designed to improve pollination during flowering, particularly when bee activity or pollination efficiency is insufficient. The company, founded in 2019, currently operates in Peru, Mexico, South Africa and Israel. Its latest Series A funding round brings total investment to $20 million (€17.2 million). The new capital will support expansion in existing markets and preparations for entering the United States, including applications in almonds and blueberries.

2 different approaches to robotic pollination

BloomX currently offers two systems, each using a different pollination technique. The Robee, developed for blueberries, mimics the buzz pollination performed by bumblebees. It applies controlled vibrations to flowers, causing the anthers to release pollen. This technique is particularly relevant for crops in which vibration helps release pollen that is otherwise difficult to extract.

The Yahav 2400, commercially launched in 2026, uses a different approach for avocado orchards. High-voltage electrodes generate a controlled electric field that attracts pollen grains and helps detach them from male flowers. The pollen is collected on a specially designed textile that mimics the surface of a bee’s body. The system then transfers the pollen to receptive female flowers. Both systems combine robotic equipment with AI-based algorithms to support pollination management.

Yield increases of 20% claimed

According to BloomX, growers using its technology have achieved average yield increases of approximately 20%, alongside improvements in fruit size and quality. The company names Agrovision in Peru, Allesbeste in South Africa and the Granot Group in Israel among its customers. BloomX also reports returns on investment of up to 10.5 times. However, the company has not provided details of the trial methodology, comparison plots or the period over which these returns were calculated. The figures therefore remain manufacturer-reported results rather than independently verified performance data. A single operator can reportedly cover up to 3.5 hectares (8.6 acres) per day. BloomX says its equipment can also operate in weather conditions that restrict bee activity, potentially extending the effective pollination window.

Pollination offered as a service

Unlike many agricultural robots sold as capital equipment, BloomX offers its technology through a Pollination-as-a-Service model. Growers pay for the pollination service rather than purchasing the machines outright. This removes the need for a substantial upfront investment, although BloomX has not disclosed its service pricing or costs per hectare. “Pollination, a critical link in fruit production, has remained entirely at the mercy of nature”, says Thai Sade, co-founder and CEO of BloomX. According to Sade, the company’s technology is intended to work alongside bees, giving growers greater control over pollination and reducing dependence on favourable conditions during flowering.

Expansion into new crops and markets

The $13 million funding round was led by Elah Fund, with participation from several existing and new investors, including the Israel Innovation Authority. BloomX plans to strengthen its position in avocado and blueberry production in Peru, Mexico, South Africa and Israel. It is also preparing to introduce its technology to US growers and investigate applications in additional crops, including almonds. For fruit growers, the main question will be whether the additional yield and fruit quality consistently justify the service costs under different growing conditions. Independent comparisons with conventional pollination practices will be important in establishing the technology’s economic value.

translationZh:
以色列农业科技公司BloomX已筹集1300万美元（1120万欧元），用于向牛油果和蓝莓种植者扩展其机器人授粉技术。该公司声称，其系统通过补充自然授粉，可使产量平均提高20%。BloomX正在拉丁美洲和南非扩张，并准备进入美国市场。

BloomX已开发出两套市售授粉系统，模仿蜜蜂在花朵之间传递花粉的方式。这些机器并非要取代自然传粉者，而是旨在开花期间改善授粉，尤其是在蜜蜂活动或授粉效率不足的情况下。该公司成立于2019年，目前业务覆盖秘鲁、墨西哥、南非和以色列。最新A轮融资使其总投资达到2000万美元（1720万欧元）。新资金将支持现有市场的扩张以及进入美国的准备工作，包括在杏仁和蓝莓上的应用。

**两种不同的机器人授粉方式**

BloomX目前提供两套系统，各采用不同的授粉技术。为蓝莓开发的Robee模仿熊蜂进行的震动授粉。它对花朵施加受控振动，使花药释放花粉。这项技术特别适用于那些通过振动有助于释放原本难以提取的花粉的作物。

Yahav 2400于2026年商业发布，为牛油果果园采用不同方法。高压电极产生受控电场，吸引花粉粒并帮助其从雄花上脱落。花粉被收集在一种特殊设计的纺织品上，该纺织品模仿蜜蜂身体的表面。然后系统将花粉转移到可授粉的雌花上。两套系统都将机器人设备与基于AI的算法相结合，以支持授粉管理。

**声称增产20%**

据BloomX称，使用其技术的种植者平均增产约20%，同时果实大小和品质也有所改善。该公司将秘鲁的Agrovision、南非的Allesbeste和以色列的Granot Group列为其客户。BloomX还报告投资回报率高达10.5倍。然而，该公司未提供试验方法、对比地块或回报计算周期的详细信息。因此，这些数据仍为制造商报告的结果，而非独立验证的性能数据。据报道，一名操作员每天可覆盖多达3.5公顷（8.6英亩）。BloomX表示，其设备还可以在限制蜜蜂活动的天气条件下运行，有可能延长有效授粉窗口。

**以服务形式提供授粉**

与许多作为资本设备销售的农业机器人不同，BloomX通过“授粉即服务”模式提供其技术。种植者为授粉服务付费，而非直接购买机器。这消除了大额前期投资的需求，尽管BloomX未披露其服务定价或每公顷成本。“授粉是水果生产中的关键环节，却完全受制于自然，”BloomX联合创始人兼CEO Thai Sade表示。据Sade称，该公司的技术旨在与蜜蜂协同工作，让种植者对授粉有更大的控制权，并减少开花期对有利条件的依赖。

**扩展新作物和新市场**

这轮1300万美元融资由Elah Fund领投，多家现有和新投资者参与，包括以色列创新局。BloomX计划加强其在秘鲁、墨西哥、南非和以色列的牛油果和蓝莓生产地位。它还准备向美国种植者引入其技术，并研究在包括杏仁在内的其他作物上的应用。对于水果种植者而言，主要问题将是额外产量和果实品质在不同种植条件下是否能持续证明服务成本的合理性。与常规授粉实践的独立比较对于确立该技术的经济价值至关重要。
